executive_result.primary_delta: The narrow P0 predicted Horus/Wedjat/Sons-of-Horus-class material around the Mendes phallus+djed body equipment. Quibell 1902 already records an explicit gold Isis-and-Horus pendant, two gold eye forms, and three of the four funerary genii inside the gold object inventory recovered from the body below the protective slab.
executive_result.important_limit: Quibell does not preserve centimeter-scale/anatomical placement for these small gold motifs relative to CG53469 or the djed. Therefore presence is promoted, but the spatial-program gate remains open.
executive_result.matched_control_result: Vernier's broader Cairo catalogue independently contains generic mummy-decoration classes such as four funerary genii, an udjat, a gold eye and falcon-sheet ornaments outside this Mendes sequence. Thus Horus/eye/genii presence alone is not unique and cannot establish a special Mendes restoration program.

SONS_OF_HORUS_CLASSIFICATION_FIREWALL.general_egyptological_control: Museum and academic descriptions commonly call Imsety, Hapi, Duamutef and Qebehsenuef the four funerary genii / Four Sons of Horus.
not_allowed: Assign individual names to the three surviving Mendes figures without iconography or inscription.
Assume the missing fourth genius was never present originally.
Treat the class identification as proof of deliberate pairing with CG53469.

VERNIER_CG53465_53475_RECHECK.source: Emile Vernier, Catalogue general du Musee du Caire, Bijoux et orfevreries, t. II, 1927
VERNIER_CG53465_53475_RECHECK.catalogue_compression_signal: Vernier explicitly groups thin metal elements used to decorate mummies and sarcophagi. Plate LXXXVII compresses the Tell Ibn es-Salam assemblage into mummy covering/collar/chest ornament/sandals/divinities/gold debris instead of preserving Quibell's complete small-object list.
mapping_limits: CG53475 falcon cannot be promoted to Horus without an inscription or object-level iconographic match.
CG53474 goddess cannot be promoted to Isis/Nephthys solely from the generic table label.
Quibell's explicit gold Isis-and-Horus, two gold eyes, three genii and djed are not yet individually bound to stable CG/JE numbers in the inspected public catalogue text.

MATCHED_CONTROL.interpretation: Eye/udjat, falcon and four-genii motifs are broader Egyptian funerary decoration classes; their mere presence in Mendes has low uniqueness.
